text: Aarav Steel Ltd reported consolidated revenue of INR 4,812 crore for Q1FY27, up 11.4% year-on-year, driven by higher realizations in flat steel products. EBITDA margin expanded to 17.2% from 15.8% in the prior year quarter, aided by softer coking coal costs.
The company's export volumes declined 6% quarter-on-quarter due to anti-dumping duties imposed by the European Union in June 2026, partially offset by stronger domestic infrastructure demand.

On the earnings call, CFO Priya Menon guided for full-year FY27 EBITDA margin in the range of 16.5% to 18%, and said capex of INR 1,200 crore for the new Odisha plant remains on track for commissioning in Q4FY27.
Promoter entity Aarav Family Trust sold 3,20,000 shares (0.42% of paid-up capital) between 25-29 August 2026 at an average price of INR 612.4, reducing promoter holding from 54.1% to 53.68%.
Management had guided in Q4FY26 for the Odisha plant to be commissioned by Q3FY27; this has now been pushed to Q4FY27, the second delay in the project's timeline since it was first announced in FY25.
Bhavani Pharma Ltd posted Q1FY27 revenue of INR 1,946 crore, up 8.1% year-on-year, with US generics business growing 14% on the back of new product launches in the injectables portfolio.

The company disclosed that its Vizag formulation facility received four observations from the US FDA following an inspection in July 2026, none classified as data integrity related; a response has been filed within the stipulated 15-day window.

CEO Rakesh Iyer stated on the call that the company expects US pricing pressure to stabilise in H2FY27 and reiterated full-year revenue growth guidance of 10-12%, while flagging that the Vizag FDA observations could delay two pending product approvals by one to two quarters.
FII holding in Bhavani Pharma Ltd increased from 18.4% to 19.9% quarter-on-quarter as of 30 June 2026, while domestic mutual fund holding was broadly flat at 12.1%.
Chandra Textiles Ltd reported a 4.3% year-on-year decline in Q1FY27 revenue to INR 812 crore, citing weak export demand from the United States and Europe amid destocking by large retail buyers.
Gross margin contracted by 220 basis points year-on-year to 28.6% due to higher cotton procurement costs and lower capacity utilisation of 71%, down from 82% in the prior year quarter.

Management said order inquiries had picked up in July 2026 and expressed cautious optimism that capacity utilisation could recover to the mid-70s percentage range by Q3FY27, but declined to give specific revenue guidance citing demand uncertainty.
Deccan Logistics Ltd reported Q1FY27 revenue of INR 1,102 crore, up 19.6% year-on-year, with the warehousing segment growing 27% driven by new e-commerce fulfilment contracts signed in FY26.

Internal freight-movement tracking shows a 9% month-on-month increase in truck volumes on Deccan Logistics-linked highway corridors in July 2026, consistent with the company's reported warehousing segment growth.

The Ministry of Road Transport's revised axle-load norms, effective 1 October 2026, are expected to marginally raise Deccan Logistics' fleet compliance costs; the company has not yet quantified the impact publicly.
